title: Root-product valuations determine a monic polynomial
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and let $K=\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its normalized absolute value [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Let $P,Q\in K[X]$ be monic polynomials of the same degree $d\geq0$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Choose an algebraic closure $\overline K$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] with the extension of this absolute value, and write $a_1,\ldots,a_d$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ for the roots of $P$ and $Q$, counted with multiplicity. If for every $F\in\mathbf Z[T]$ one has
$$\left|\prod_{i=1}^dF(a_i)\right|_\ell=\left|\prod_{i=1}^dF(b_i)\right|_\ell,$$
then $P=Q$. Products and absolute values are computed in $\overline K$; the empty product is $1$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.21 and its proof, printed p.51.

proof.text: If $d=0$, monicity gives $P=Q=1$. Henceforth $d>0$. First extend the test identity to $F\in\mathbf Q[T]$. Choose an integer $N>0$ clearing the finitely many coefficient denominators, so $NF\in\mathbf Z[T]$. Each side of the identity for $NF$ is $|N|_\ell^d$ times the corresponding side for $F$. Since $|N|_\ell>0$, cancellation proves the identity for $F$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.21 and proof, printed p.51.

proof.text:
Extend next to $F=\sum_{j=0}^s u_jT^j\in K[T]$. By the rational-density clause of [lem-sfb-padic-minpoly-normed-separation], choose rational coefficients $u_{j,n}$ with $|u_{j,n}-u_j|_\ell<1/n$ for $n\geq1$, and put $F_n=\sum_{j=0}^s u_{j,n}T^j$. The given absolute value in the closure is nonarchimedean by [lem-sfb-ultrametric-criterion-natural-norms]: every natural number is in $K$ and has absolute value at most $1$ by [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Thus for each listed root $c$,
$$|F_n(c)-F(c)|\leq n^{-1}\max(1,|c|)^s.$$
Consequently $F_n(c)\to F(c)$. Products converge too: expand $\prod x_i-\prod y_i$ as the sum of terms $(x_i-y_i)\prod_{j<i}x_j\prod_{j>i}y_j$; the other factors are bounded. Finally $\big||u|-|v|\big|\leq|u-v|$ shows convergence of the product absolute values. Taking real limits in the identity for $F_n$ proves the identity for $F$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.21 and proof, printed p.51.

proof.text: Fix $\alpha\in\overline K$ and let $f\in K[T]$ be its minimal polynomial. The minimal-polynomial clause of [lem-sfb-padic-minpoly-normed-separation] gives $m=\deg f\geq1$. Apply step 2 to $f$ and apply [lem-sfb-padic-minpoly-root-product] separately to $H=P$ and $H=Q$. It gives $|P(\alpha)|^m=|Q(\alpha)|^m$. Nonnegative real $m$th powers are injective for $m>0$ (if $0\leq u<v$, multiplying the strict inequality, or dividing by $v>0$, gives $u^m<v^m$). Hence $|P(\alpha)|=|Q(\alpha)|$ for every $\alpha$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.21 and proof, printed p.51.

proof.text:
Let $x$ occur in either root list and let $e,f$ be its numbers of occurrences in the lists for $P,Q$. By [lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization] and monicity, these lists factor $P,Q$ as products of $X-c$ with their stated multiplicities. Let $C_P=\prod_{a_i
e x}|x-a_i|$ and $C_Q=\prod_{b_i
e x}|x-b_i|$; both are positive, including empty products. Take $r>0$ smaller than every nonzero distance from $x$ to a listed root, using $r=1$ if there are none. For all sufficiently large integers $n$, put $\alpha_n=x+\ell^n$, so $0<|\alpha_n-x|=\ell^{-n}<r$. For $c
e x$, the strong triangle inequality gives $|\alpha_n-c|\leq|x-c|$, and the reverse inequality follows from $x-c=(x-\alpha_n)+(\alpha_n-c)$: a strict decrease would contradict $|x-c|\leq\max(\ell^{-n},|\alpha_n-c|)$. Thus
$$|P(\alpha_n)|=C_P\ell^{-ne},\qquad |Q(\alpha_n)|=C_Q\ell^{-nf}.$$
Apply step 3 for two successive large integers $n,n+1$ and divide the positive equalities. This yields $\ell^{-e}=\ell^{-f}$, whence $e=f$, since $\ell\geq2$. Therefore every root in the union of the two finite lists has equal multiplicity. Reorder the lists and use their monic factorizations to obtain $P=Q$ in $\overline K[X]$, hence in $K[X]$ since its inclusion into the closure is injective.
